THR-01.statement: Attacker-controlled input changes interpreter commands or output structure.
THR-01.boundaries: HTTP requests, stored data and browser output

THR-02.statement: Invalid input, workflow abuse or races bypass business invariants.
THR-02.boundaries: Untrusted input to state-changing feature handlers

THR-03.statement: Browser-origin or script attacks steal sessions or perform unauthorized actions.
THR-03.assets: Razor, React, BFF and response headers
THR-03.boundaries: Browser to issuer/BFF and third-party content

THR-04.statement: Ambiguous HTTP messages or exposed service protocols bypass validation.
THR-04.boundaries: Client and proxy to service endpoints

THR-05.statement: Untrusted file content or paths expose files or execute unintended content.
THR-05.assets: File configuration, key ring and exports
THR-05.boundaries: Operator/user file input to storage and downloads

THR-06.statement: Credential theft, guessing or recovery abuse impersonates an account.
THR-06.boundaries: Browser/IdP to authentication and recovery stores

THR-07.statement: Stolen, stale or fixed sessions retain unauthorized access.
THR-07.boundaries: Browser cookies and distributed session stores

THR-08.statement: Privilege escalation or stale policy permits forbidden operations.

THR-09.statement: Forged, mis-scoped or wrong-purpose tokens are accepted.
THR-09.boundaries: Issuer to client and resource server trust boundary

THR-10.statement: Protocol mix-up, replay or client confusion exposes identity or access.
THR-10.boundaries: Issuer, relying party, resource server and browser

THR-11.statement: Weak, reused or exposed cryptographic material compromises protected data.

THR-12.statement: Network interception or peer impersonation breaks confidentiality and trust.

THR-13.statement: Unsafe configuration, secret handling or exposed diagnostics enables compromise.
THR-13.boundaries: Operator/deployment to application and dependency configuration

THR-14.statement: Excessive collection, retention or disclosure exposes personal/sensitive data.
THR-14.boundaries: Application to browser, persistence, audit and export

THR-15.statement: Unsafe dependencies, coding practices or concurrent operations undermine controls.

THR-16.statement: Missing, tampered or sensitive logs hide attacks or expose secrets.
THR-16.assets: Security logging, audit and error handling
THR-16.boundaries: Security events and failures to logs/audit operators

THR-17.statement: Unreviewed real-time media/signaling surfaces could expose data or relay access.
THR-17.boundaries: Conditional WebRTC media, signaling and relay boundaries
